quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. This sign warns drivers that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This lets you blend in safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets. Signal 5 seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: What should drivers do when crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to let you go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before driving onto a sidewalk. Pedestrians and traffic on the road have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A group is picking up trash along the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as the traffic direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they face the traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Warning signs for curves and turns often have an advisory speed sign attached. This speed is recommended for good conditions. Never ignore these speeds in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: How many driving hours must an applicant under 18 complete before getting a probationary license?
questions.explanation: Applicants under 18 must complete 30 hours of driving. 10 of these hours must be at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Making a right turn here is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: You and the driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: What message is on this yellow pennant-shaped sign?
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs warn drivers that they are in a no passing zone.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
You must move completely into the left lane when passing a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights always turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles use the full width of a lane. Your entire vehicle must be in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.
You will need to turn left soon.

questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the road's edge. When this line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic control signs, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without a stop sign or traffic signal, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be prepared to yield to avoid a crash. Release the accelerator, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body will be pushed backward. Press yourself against the seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to stop being pushed into another vehicle.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: On a road with no curb, turn your wheels so your vehicle rolls away from traffic if your brakes fail. This applies whether parking uphill or downhill.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and carefully drive through.
Turn right or left since the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. After stopping, you may go when the way is clear.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you turn?
questions.explanation: When turning, go from your current lane into the first available legal lane in the direction you are turning. On a left turn onto a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up level with the car in front of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up level with the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop next to the car directly in front of your desired parking space. Then turn your wheels to begin parking.

questions.question: You are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway. What should you do?
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless passing or turning left. On an interstate, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are white with black markings. All drivers must obey them.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be fixed in one place or moving (like vehicles marking lanes or snow removal). They are marked with orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Watch for other drivers entering your lane. Never change lanes or pass in an intersection.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs indicate:
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the law.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a:
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means stop, just like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly with caution. Look both ways before crossing.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Increase their speed to reach their final destination more quickly.

questions.explanation: In bad weather and on wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: This white sign means:

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and prepare to stop at the crossing if necessary.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Braking can make the skid worse.

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: If it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car ahead is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: For drivers 21 years old or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 or older, the legal limit is a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drunk driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Go ahead because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they plan to:
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand extended downward means the driver is stopping. If you are following this driver, adjust your driving accordingly.

questions.question: When can you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: It is appropriate to use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you complete the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete your turn into the leftmost lane.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Drive slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match the traffic speed. Signal, look for an opening, then merge safely.

questions.question: When should you give up your legal right-of-way?
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent collisions.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in residential and business areas with no posted speed limits?
questions.explanation: Unless there is a posted sign, the speed limit on residential and business streets is 25 miles per hour.

questions.question: If you don't see a gap in traffic when entering the freeway, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you don't see a gap, slow down on the ramp to wait for one. Do not stop at the end of the ramp or you won't have room to speed up before entering the highway.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These factors change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should finish the turn in:

options.text: The lane closest to your starting lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your starting lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: When parallel parking downhill, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the curb or edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light braking pressure.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used on traffic signals.
It means the same as a yellow traffic light.
You may turn in the direction the arrow points.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow traffic light. Reduce your speed and prepare to stop.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to watch for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to watch for hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means constantly looking ahead for potential hazards. Staring only at the road directly in front is dangerous. Scan the road and be alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, try to move right. Steering left is dangerous because if the other driver corrects, you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: Warning signs are most commonly which color?
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about conditions that may not be obvious.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead becomes a divided highway. Stay to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then speed up again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, move to a different lane if possible. If you cannot move over, slowly reduce your speed. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.
